07.title: Tables, rows and keys
07.intro: Run these in order, just like in the lecture. Click one to load it, then press Run.

steps.label: Everything in the customers table
steps.sql: SELECT * FROM customers;

steps.label: Only the customer with id 2
steps.sql: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE id = 2;

steps.label: The table's structure
steps.sql: \d customers

steps.label: A second Grace: same name, new key
steps.sql: INSERT INTO customers VALUES (4, 'Grace', 'London');

steps.label: Look again: two Graces, two keys
steps.sql: SELECT * FROM customers;

steps.label: A second customer with id 2?
steps.sql: INSERT INTO customers VALUES (2, 'Linus', 'Helsinki');

steps.label: A customer without an id?
steps.sql: INSERT INTO customers VALUES (NULL, 'Linus', 'Helsinki');

steps.label: A price that is not a number?
steps.sql: INSERT INTO products VALUES (5, 'Mug', 'cheap', 'home');

steps.label: All tables of the shop
steps.sql: \dt

steps.label: The products
steps.sql: SELECT * FROM products;

steps.label: The orders
steps.sql: SELECT * FROM orders;

exercise.task: Add yourself to the shop as customer 5, with your own city. Then try to add a friend with the same id. What does the database say, and how do you get your friend in?
exercise.answer: INSERT INTO customers VALUES (5, 'Your name', 'Your city'); works. The same id again is refused: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "customers_pkey". Give your friend a new key, for example 6.

08a.title: Asking questions with SQL
08a.intro: Run these in order, just like in the lecture. Click one to load it, then press Run. Then change them: other columns, other tests, other orders.

steps.label: Name and city of every customer
steps.sql: SELECT name, city FROM customers;

steps.label: Price with tax, rounded
steps.sql: SELECT name, price, round(price * 1.19, 2) AS with_tax FROM products;

steps.label: Products over 20
steps.sql: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price > 20;

steps.label: The trap: AND before OR
steps.sql: SELECT name, category, price FROM products WHERE category = 'home' OR category = 'travel' AND price < 20;

steps.label: The same with brackets
steps.sql: SELECT name, category, price FROM products WHERE (category = 'home' OR category = 'travel') AND price < 20;

steps.label: Customers in three cities
steps.sql: SELECT name, city FROM customers WHERE city IN ('London', 'Boston', 'Helsinki');

steps.label: Prices between 5 and 25 (both ends count)
steps.sql: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 5 AND 25;

steps.label: The three most expensive products
steps.sql: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 3;

exercise.task: Find all orders from March 2025 with a quantity of more than 2, newest first.
exercise.answer: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE ordered_on BETWEEN '2025-03-01' AND '2025-03-31' AND quantity > 2 ORDER BY ordered_on DESC;  gives orders 12, 9, 6 and 3.

08b.title: SQL: text and missing values
08b.intro: Run these in order, just like in the lecture. Click one to load it, then press Run. Then try your own patterns and NULL tests.

steps.label: The puzzle: not in London
steps.sql: SELECT name, city FROM customers WHERE city <> 'London';

steps.label: Second letter d
steps.sql: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE name LIKE '_d%';

steps.label: ILIKE ignores capital letters
steps.sql: SELECT name, city FROM customers WHERE city ILIKE 'london';

steps.label: A label: name and category
steps.sql: SELECT name || ' (' || category || ')' AS label FROM products;

steps.label: = NULL finds nothing
steps.sql: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE city = NULL;

steps.label: IS NULL
steps.sql: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE city IS NULL;

steps.label: coalesce: unknown instead of nothing
steps.sql: SELECT name, coalesce(city, 'unknown') AS city FROM customers;

steps.label: The distinct cities, sorted
steps.sql: SELECT DISTINCT city FROM customers ORDER BY city;

exercise.task: Find every customer whose name ends in a small 'a', or who has no city at all. Show the word 'unknown' instead of an empty city.
exercise.answer: SELECT name, coalesce(city, 'unknown') AS city FROM customers WHERE name LIKE '%a' OR city IS NULL;  gives Ada (London), Barbara (unknown) and Katherine (unknown).
